raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Description

Enable v2 Megatron/SGLang AWEX colocation on the shared adapters introduced in #1684. Actor and rollout workers can share GPUs while retaining separate training and inference parallel layouts.

The controller coordinates rollout pause/drain, inference memory release, auxiliary-model scoring, training, checkpointing, and weight publication. Rollout memory is released before reference-model scoring, and generation resumes only after the updated weights and policy version are committed. CUDA IPC exports remain alive until receiver acknowledgement.

Support synchronous and asynchronous DCP recovery through the existing checkpoint generation and `LATEST` protocol. Asynchronous saves publish `LATEST` only after finalization. Before shutdown, v2 controllers drain pending saves on every training rank before destroying workers or their parent rollout guards. Drain failures propagate instead of proceeding with cleanup. This lifecycle applies to both colocated and separated v2 Megatron training.

## Related Issue

Builds on #1684 (shared AWEX adapters and converters).

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix
- [x] ✨ New feature
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ♻️ Refactoring
- [ ] ⚡ Performance improvement
- [ ] ✅ Test coverage improvement

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/areal-project/community/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (`pre-commit run --all-files`)
- [x] Relevant tests pass; new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Documentation updated (built with `./docs/build_all.sh`)
- [x] Branch is up to date with `main`
- [ ] Self-reviewed via `/review-pr` command
- [ ] This PR was created by a coding agent via `/create-pr`
- [ ] This PR is a breaking change

**Breaking Change Details (if applicable):**

No intentional breaking changes to supported v1 or v2 separated weight-update paths.

## Additional Context

Validation:

- CPU regression suite after test consolidation: **489 passed, 45 skipped**, including **10 `LATEST` pointer tests**.
- Real-CUDA IPC lifetime tests: **6 passed**, covering acknowledgements, failures, timeouts, repeated publication, and teardown protection.
- **Colocated, two GPUs:** Qwen3-0.6B, actor DP2, rollout TP2, reference scoring, KL=0.01. Both synchronous and asynchronous DCP runs completed 20 training steps, restarted through `LATEST`, and completed steps 21–22.
- **Separated, four GPUs:** Qwen3-0.6B, actor on one GPU, reference model on one GPU, rollout TP2 on the other two. With KL=0.01 and asynchronous DCP enabled, the run completed the same 20-step/restart/2-step sequence.
- Each async run finalized four checkpoints. The final save was still pending at training completion and was drained before worker cleanup. Restart restored model, optimizer, LR scheduler, and RNG state. Both async jobs exited successfully; all 22 steps reported successful optimizer steps and finite, nonzero gradient norms. Learning rate was zero on the first warmup step and nonzero thereafter.
- Tested with PyTorch 2.9.1+cu129, SGLang 0.5.10.post1, Megatron-Core 0.19.0, the Megatron-Bridge 0.6.0 wheel pinned in `uv.lock`, AWEX 0.9.0, and torch-memory-saver 0.0.9.
- Full pre-commit checks and English/Chinese documentation builds passed.

Scope and validation limits:

- AWEX colocation supports full-weight Megatron training and SGLang inference. Ray v2 guard colocation, LoRA colocation, and other training/inference backends are outside this PR's supported scope.
- GPU end-to-end tests used a single node and the local scheduler. Slurm guard placement has CPU regression coverage; no new multi-node GPU run was performed. Auxiliary guard colocation onto a partial-node actor allocation remains restricted; the four-GPU test used a dedicated reference GPU.
- Pointer tests cover atomic selection, ignoring unpublished generations, invalid-pointer rejection, and publication failure propagation. The GPU runs exercised normal shutdown and restart, **not mid-write SIGKILL or ENOSPC fault injection**.
- The subsequent LoRA preflight, incomplete drain-probe, and concurrent session-initialization, and initialization/teardown lifecycle fixes passed CPU regression tests; the GPU end-to-end runs preceded these boundary fixes.
- Both v1 and v2 reject incompatible rollout allocator settings without rewriting them. Configure `expandable_segments:False` (or omit the option) in both allocator environment names for rollout; actor settings remain independent. Startup rejection and example configuration parsing passed CPU checks; no new GPU run was performed for this policy change.
- These short-generation GSM8K runs validate the execution and recovery lifecycle, not learning quality or performance improvements.
- Based on main commit `3b93679888e9f4929f6f155f13c6a286a62dfd72`, verified as the upstream tip when publishing.

Thank you for your contribution!

The text counts the number of GPUs for the target guard based on target_worker.spec.gpu, but actor guards derived from rollout guards inherit the parent guard's spec, even if only one GPU is actually bound. When auxiliary guards are co-located with actors, this leads to an overestimation of the total GPU count and rejects valid topologies.

         strategy = job.scheduling_strategy
         strategy_type = SchedulingStrategyType(strategy.type)
         colocate_role = strategy.target
+        is_v2_guard_colocation = is_v2_training_guard_colocation(
+            role, strategy, schedulings[0].cmd
+        )
         logger.info(

             f"(strategy: {strategy_type}, colocate_with: {colocate_role})"
         )
 
+        if is_v2_guard_colocation:
+            if not colocate_role:
+                raise WorkerCreationError(
+                    role,
+                    "Invalid strategy",
+                    "Colocation strategy requires target role to be specified",
+                )
+            # v2 services register workers under derived role names: the
+            # inference service uses "<role>-inf" and the training service
+            # uses "<role>-guard". Resolve whichever the target published.
+            # The train controller initializes in a background pipeline that
+            # may reach this point before the rollout stack has registered
+            # its workers, so poll instead of failing immediately.
+            target_candidates = [
+                f"{colocate_role}-inf",
+                f"{colocate_role}-guard",
+                colocate_role,
+            ]
+            target_role = None
+            wait_deadline = time.monotonic() + 600.0
+            while time.monotonic() < wait_deadline:
+                target_role = next(
+                    (r for r in target_candidates if r in self._workers), None
+                )
+                if target_role is not None:
+                    break
+                logger.info(
+                    "v2 guard colocation: waiting for target role "
+                    f"(one of {target_candidates}) to register workers..."
+                )
+                time.sleep(5.0)
+            if target_role is None:
+                raise WorkerNotFoundError(
+                    f"Cannot colocate v2 guards with role '{colocate_role}' - "
+                    f"none of {target_candidates} appeared within 600s"
+                )
+
+            # get_workers blocks until the target guards are fully ready
+            # (ports registered); forking earlier hits empty worker_ports.
+            self.get_workers(role=target_role, timeout=600.0)
+            target_workers = self._workers[target_role]
+            target_gpus_by_host: dict[str, int] = {}
+            parent_workers: list[SlurmWorkerInfo] = []
+            fork_envs: list[dict[str, str]] = []
+            base_env = dict(schedulings[0].env_vars or {})
+            # A target guard fronts spec.gpu GPUs. Expand one forked worker
+            # per GPU and pin each to its node-local physical slot: guards on
+            # a host are laid out contiguously in worker order (the same
+            # base-gpu ordering the inference servers were forked with), so
+            # slot = host-running-base + within-guard offset. rank%N guessing
+            # breaks whenever guard count != GPU count (e.g. tp>1 servers).
+            host_base: dict[str, int] = {}
+            target_layout: list[tuple[int, str, SlurmWorkerInfo]] = []
+            for target_worker in target_workers:
+                target_gpu_count = target_worker.spec.gpu if target_worker.spec else 0

raw_graphql_pull_request.title: feat(v2): support AWEX colocation and async checkpoint recovery

repo.description: The RL Bridge for LLM-based Agent Applications. Made Simple & Flexible.
repo.name: AReaL

detail.body:
## Description

Enable v2 Megatron/SGLang AWEX colocation on the shared adapters introduced in #1684. Actor and rollout workers can share GPUs while retaining separate training and inference parallel layouts.

The controller coordinates rollout pause/drain, inference memory release, auxiliary-model scoring, training, checkpointing, and weight publication. Rollout memory is released before reference-model scoring, and generation resumes only after the updated weights and policy version are committed. CUDA IPC exports remain alive until receiver acknowledgement.

Support synchronous and asynchronous DCP recovery through the existing checkpoint generation and `LATEST` protocol. Asynchronous saves publish `LATEST` only after finalization. Before shutdown, v2 controllers drain pending saves on every training rank before destroying workers or their parent rollout guards. Drain failures propagate instead of proceeding with cleanup. This lifecycle applies to both colocated and separated v2 Megatron training.

## Related Issue

Builds on #1684 (shared AWEX adapters and converters).

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix
- [x] ✨ New feature
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ♻️ Refactoring
- [ ] ⚡ Performance improvement
- [ ] ✅ Test coverage improvement

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/areal-project/community/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (`pre-commit run --all-files`)
- [x] Relevant tests pass; new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Documentation updated (built with `./docs/build_all.sh`)
- [x] Branch is up to date with `main`
- [ ] Self-reviewed via `/review-pr` command
- [ ] This PR was created by a coding agent via `/create-pr`
- [ ] This PR is a breaking change

**Breaking Change Details (if applicable):**

No intentional breaking changes to supported v1 or v2 separated weight-update paths.

## Additional Context

Validation:

- CPU regression suite after test consolidation: **489 passed, 45 skipped**, including **10 `LATEST` pointer tests**.
- Real-CUDA IPC lifetime tests: **6 passed**, covering acknowledgements, failures, timeouts, repeated publication, and teardown protection.
- **Colocated, two GPUs:** Qwen3-0.6B, actor DP2, rollout TP2, reference scoring, KL=0.01. Both synchronous and asynchronous DCP runs completed 20 training steps, restarted through `LATEST`, and completed steps 21–22.
- **Separated, four GPUs:** Qwen3-0.6B, actor on one GPU, reference model on one GPU, rollout TP2 on the other two. With KL=0.01 and asynchronous DCP enabled, the run completed the same 20-step/restart/2-step sequence.
- Each async run finalized four checkpoints. The final save was still pending at training completion and was drained before worker cleanup. Restart restored model, optimizer, LR scheduler, and RNG state. Both async jobs exited successfully; all 22 steps reported successful optimizer steps and finite, nonzero gradient norms. Learning rate was zero on the first warmup step and nonzero thereafter.
- Tested with PyTorch 2.9.1+cu129, SGLang 0.5.10.post1, Megatron-Core 0.19.0, the Megatron-Bridge 0.6.0 wheel pinned in `uv.lock`, AWEX 0.9.0, and torch-memory-saver 0.0.9.
- Full pre-commit checks and English/Chinese documentation builds passed.

Scope and validation limits:

- AWEX colocation supports full-weight Megatron training and SGLang inference. Ray v2 guard colocation, LoRA colocation, and other training/inference backends are outside this PR's supported scope.
- GPU end-to-end tests used a single node and the local scheduler. Slurm guard placement has CPU regression coverage; no new multi-node GPU run was performed. Auxiliary guard colocation onto a partial-node actor allocation remains restricted; the four-GPU test used a dedicated reference GPU.
- Pointer tests cover atomic selection, ignoring unpublished generations, invalid-pointer rejection, and publication failure propagation. The GPU runs exercised normal shutdown and restart, **not mid-write SIGKILL or ENOSPC fault injection**.
- The subsequent LoRA preflight, incomplete drain-probe, and concurrent session-initialization, and initialization/teardown lifecycle fixes passed CPU regression tests; the GPU end-to-end runs preceded these boundary fixes.
- Both v1 and v2 reject incompatible rollout allocator settings without rewriting them. Configure `expandable_segments:False` (or omit the option) in both allocator environment names for rollout; actor settings remain independent. Startup rejection and example configuration parsing passed CPU checks; no new GPU run was performed for this policy change.
- These short-generation GSM8K runs validate the execution and recovery lifecycle, not learning quality or performance improvements.
- Based on main commit `3b93679888e9f4929f6f155f13c6a286a62dfd72`, verified as the upstream tip when publishing.

+def validate_colocated_device_namespace(
+    visible_devices: str | None, base: int, count: int
+) -> None:
+    """Reject layouts that cannot use the full-node numeric GPU mapping."""
+    expected = [str(device) for device in range(base, base + count)]
+    actual = (
+        [device.strip() for device in visible_devices.split(",")]
+        if visible_devices is not None
+        else []
+    )
+    if actual != expected:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "V2 Slurm colocation requires contiguous numeric CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES "
+            f"matching its full-node placement; expected {expected}, got {actual}"
+        )
+
+
+def is_v2_training_guard_colocation(
+    role: str, strategy: SchedulingStrategy | None, command: str | None
+) -> bool:
+    """Identify the v2 training guard path without matching other services."""
+    if not is_colocation_strategy(strategy) or not role.endswith("-guard"):
+        return False
+    try:
+        command_parts = shlex.split(command or "")
+    except ValueError:
+        return False
+    if "-m" not in command_parts:
+        return False
+    module_index = command_parts.index("-m") + 1
+    return (
+        module_index < len(command_parts)
+        and command_parts[module_index] == "areal.v2.training_service.guard"
+    )
+
+
+def colocated_gpu_rank_key(
+    host: str, device_id: int, local_rank: int
+) -> tuple[int, str, int]:
+    """Return the canonical rank key shared by schedulers and the gateway."""
+    return device_id - local_rank, host, local_rank
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ColocatedGpuSlot:
+    """A physical GPU slot in the canonical colocated rank order."""
+
+    group_index: int
+    host: str
+    device_id: int
+    local_rank: int
+
+
+def canonical_colocated_gpu_slots(
+    groups: Sequence[tuple[str, Sequence[str]]],
+) -> list[ColocatedGpuSlot]:
+    """Order physical GPU slots like the weight-update gateway.
+
+    Each input group represents one inference server and must list contiguous
+    node-local devices in local-rank order. The returned order uses server base
+    device first, then host and local rank, so it is independent of scheduler
+    worker creation order.
+    """
+    slots: list[ColocatedGpuSlot] = []
+    seen_devices: set[tuple[str, int]] = set()
+    for group_index, (host, raw_devices) in enumerate(groups):
+        if not host:
+            raise ValueError(f"GPU group {group_index} has no host")
+        try:
+            devices = [int(device) for device in raw_devices]
+        except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"GPU group {group_index} has non-numeric devices: {raw_devices}"
+            ) from e
+        if not devices:
+            raise ValueError(f"GPU group {group_index} has no devices")
+
+        expected = list(range(devices[0], devices[0] + len(devices)))
+        if devices != expected:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"GPU group {group_index} devices must be contiguous in local-rank "
+                f"order, got {devices}"
+            )
+
+        for local_rank, device_id in enumerate(devices):
+            device = (host, device_id)
+            if device in seen_devices:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Physical GPU {host}:{device_id} belongs to multiple groups"
+                )
+            seen_devices.add(device)
+            slots.append(
+                ColocatedGpuSlot(
+                    group_index=group_index,
+                    host=host,
+                    device_id=device_id,
+                    local_rank=local_rank,
+                )
+            )
+

+            slot.host, slot.device_id, slot.local_rank

+# V2 AWEX colocation
+
+V2 colocation lets Megatron training workers and SGLang inference workers share GPUs. It
+uses the shared AWEX adapters and converters; placement selects the colocated memory and
+transfer lifecycle.
+
+## Supported configurations
+
+| Component           | Supported configuration                                                    |
+| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Training            | Megatron, full weights                                                     |
+| Inference           | SGLang with `enable_memory_saver: true`                                    |
+| Placement           | Local scheduler, or full-node Slurm allocations                            |
+| Slurm GPU namespace | Contiguous numeric device IDs matching the guard placement                 |
+| Checkpoints         | HF export and synchronous/asynchronous DCP recovery                        |
+| Unsupported         | LoRA colocation, FSDP colocation, vLLM colocation, Ray v2 guard colocation |
+
+UUID, reordered, or partial-node Slurm GPU allocations are rejected before training
+guards are forked. Existing v1 colocation and v2 separated weight updates keep their own
+placement and transfer paths.
+
+Use `actor._version: v2` and `rollout._version: v2`, select Megatron and SGLang
+backends, and configure actor colocation with the rollout guards. The actor and rollout
+must cover the same physical GPUs. Their parallel layouts may differ, but every SGLang
+TP/PP group must fit the supported node-local placement. Set
+`actor.megatron.async_save: true` to overlap DCP disk writes with training.
+
+## Allocator configuration
+
+TMS 0.0.9 and 0.0.10 reject `expandable_segments:True`. Both v1 and v2 AWEX rollout
+startup validate allocator settings without rewriting the environment. Configure the
+rollout role independently from the actor, for example in each `rollout.scheduling_spec`
+entry's `env_vars`:
+
+```yaml
+PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF: expandable_segments:False
+PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF: expandable_segments:False
+```
+
+PyTorch 2.9 prefers `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`, but TMS also checks the legacy
+`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` directly. Neither variable may enable expandable segments in
+the rollout process. Omitting that option is also valid. Actor allocator settings can
+remain independent. GPU masks must retain ascending, contiguous device order; reordered
+masks are rejected rather than sorted.
+
+## Memory ownership
+
+Initialization creates rollout guards, initializes training workers, and releases
+training memory before loading SGLang. Auxiliary models initialize after that release.
+Offloaded v2 auxiliary models require Megatron and use its explicit weight residency
+manager rather than the inherited inference TMS hook.
+
+Each training phase pauses rollout submission, drains generation, and releases rollout
+weights, KV cache, and CUDA graphs. Reference, critic, and teacher scoring run before
+actor memory is restored. The actor then trains, saves checkpoints, publishes weights,
+and commits the policy version. Training memory is released before inference memory is
+restored.
+
+An incomplete weight transfer or version commit leaves generation paused. Exported CUDA
+IPC storage stays alive until the reader acknowledges consumption; an unacknowledged
+export also blocks another publication or adapter teardown. After the final training
+step, inference may serve evaluation, but the rollout dispatcher does not start another
+training batch.
+
+## Recovery
+
+DCP recovery uses the same immutable checkpoint generations and `LATEST` publication
+protocol as other supported training paths. Restore loads the selected generation inside
+the colocated training phase, reuses the existing gateway, publishes the recovered
+weights, and commits the recovered version before resuming generation. Checkpoint
+corruption or a failed restore does not silently resume training.
+
+Asynchronous saves stage their payload before returning, so subsequent weight updates
+and offload do not modify the saved snapshot. `LATEST` is published only after the
+background save finalizes. Normal shutdown drains every training rank before destroying
+workers or their parent rollout guards. The drain uses `actor.request_timeout` (or the
+corresponding critic setting), which must cover the longest expected checkpoint write. A
+failed or timed-out drain raises and preserves worker resources for diagnosis; it does
+not report a successful shutdown. Abrupt process termination may leave an unpublished
+generation; recovery continues to select the last successfully published checkpoint.

+# V2 AWEX 共卡
+
+V2 共卡允许 Megatron 训练 worker 和 SGLang 推理 worker 共享 GPU。它复用统一的 AWEX adapter 与
+converter，由部署方式选择共卡显存交接及权重传输流程。
+
+## 支持范围
+
+| 组件           | 支持的配置                                         |
+| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
+| 训练           | Megatron，全量权重                                 |
+| 推理           | SGLang，开启 `enable_memory_saver: true`           |
+| 调度           | Local scheduler，或 Slurm 整节点 GPU 分配          |
+| Slurm GPU 编号 | 与 guard 布局一致的连续数字编号                    |
+| Checkpoint     | HF 导出及同步／异步 DCP 恢复                       |
+| 暂不支持       | LoRA 共卡、FSDP 共卡、vLLM 共卡、Ray v2 guard 共卡 |
+
+Slurm 分配使用 UUID、重排编号或部分节点 GPU 时，会在 fork 训练 guard 前拒绝启动。 现有 v1 共卡及 v2 分卡继续使用各自的部署和传输路径。
+
+设置 `actor._version: v2`、`rollout._version: v2`，选择 Megatron 和 SGLang 后端， 并将 actor 配置为与
+rollout guard 共卡。两侧必须覆盖相同的物理 GPU。训练和推理 并行布局可以不同，但每个 SGLang TP/PP 组必须满足支持的节点内布局。 设置
+`actor.megatron.async_save: true` 可使 DCP 磁盘写入与训练重叠。
+
+## Allocator 配置
+
+TMS 0.0.9 和 0.0.10 明确拒绝 `expandable_segments:True`。v1/v2 AWEX rollout
+启动时使用统一校验，不会自动改写环境变量。 rollout 应独立于 actor 配置，例如在各个 `rollout.scheduling_spec` 条目的
+`env_vars` 中设置：
+
+```yaml
+PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF: expandable_segments:False
+PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF: expandable_segments:False
+```
+
+PyTorch 2.9 优先读取 `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`，但 TMS 仍会直接检查旧变量 `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`，因此
+rollout 中两个变量均不能开启 expandable segments。 也可以移除该选项；actor 的 allocator 配置可以独立保留。GPU mask
+必须按升序连续排列，重排编号会明确报错，不再自动排序。
+
+## 显存交接
+
+初始化时先创建 rollout guard、初始化训练 worker，然后释放训练显存，再加载辅助模型和 SGLang。 需要 offload 的 v2 辅助模型须使用
+Megatron，通过显式权重驻留管理器释放显存， 不依赖从推理进程继承的 TMS hook。
+
+每次训练先暂停 rollout 提交并等待生成结束，释放 rollout 权重、KV cache 和 CUDA graph。 ref、critic、teacher 评分在
+actor 恢复显存之前执行。随后 actor 训练、保存 checkpoint、 发布权重并提交 policy version；释放训练显存后，才恢复推理显存。
+
+权重传输或版本提交未成功时，生成保持暂停。导出的 CUDA IPC storage 会保留到 reader 确认消费完成；未确认的导出也会阻止再次发布及 adapter
+teardown。最后一步训练后， 推理服务仍可用于评估，但 rollout dispatcher 不会启动下一批训练采样。
+
+## 恢复
+
+DCP 恢复沿用不可变 checkpoint generation 和 `LATEST` 发布协议。恢复过程在 共卡训练阶段内加载选定 generation，复用已有
+gateway，发布恢复后的权重并提交版本， 然后重新开放生成。checkpoint 损坏或恢复失败不会静默继续训练。
+
+异步保存返回前完成 CPU payload staging，后续权重更新及 offload 不会修改保存快照。后台保存 finalize 成功后才发布 `LATEST`。
+正常退出先等待所有训练 rank 的异步保存完成，再销毁 worker 及其父 rollout guard。等待使用
+`actor.request_timeout`（critic 使用对应配置），应覆盖最长预期 checkpoint 写入时间。 等待失败或超时会抛错并保留 worker
+资源供诊断，不报告成功退出。进程突然终止可能留下未发布的 generation；恢复仍选择最后成功发布的 checkpoint。

+        events.append("continue")

+        if fail_actor_release and op == "release_memory":

+    return controller

+        transactional=True,
+    )

+        lambda *args: source,
+    )

+
+def _make_handler(events):
+    handler = object.__new__(RecoverHandler)
+    handler.config = SimpleNamespace(
+        mode="auto",
+        experiment_name="exp",
+        trial_name="trial",
+        fileroot="/tmp/does-not-matter",
+    )
+    handler.freq_ctl = SimpleNamespace(load_state_dict=lambda _d: None)
+    handler._load_checkpoint = lambda engine_, path, name="default": events.append(
+        ("load_checkpoint", name)
+    )
+    return handler
+
+
+def _make_rollout(events):
+    def rec(name):
+        def _fn(*args, **kwargs):
+            tags = kwargs.get("tags", args[0] if args else None)
+            events.append((name, tuple(tags)) if tags is not None else name)
+
+        return _fn
+
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        pause=rec("pause"),
+        resume=rec("resume"),
+        pause_generation_sync=rec("pause_generation_sync"),
+        continue_generation=rec("continue_generation"),
+        offload=rec("offload"),
+        onload=rec("onload"),
+        set_version=lambda v: events.append(("rollout_set_version", v)),
+    )
+
+
+def _make_actor(events, rollout, colocate=True):
+    from areal.v2.training_service.controller.controller import (
+        GatewayTrainController,
+    )
+
+    actor = object.__new__(GatewayTrainController)
+    actor._colocate = colocate
+    actor.rollout = rollout
+    actor._broadcast_awex_memory_op = lambda op, tags: events.append(
+        ("awex", op, tuple(tags))
+    )
+    actor.connect_engine = lambda r, m: events.append("connect_engine")
+
+    def update_weights(meta):
+        actor._colocate_update_started = True
+        actor._colocate_transfer_succeeded = True
+        events.append(("update_weights", meta.version))
+        actor._colocate_update_succeeded = False
+
+    actor.update_weights = update_weights
+    actor.set_version = lambda v: events.append(("actor_set_version", v))
+
+    def mark_committed():
+        events.append("mark_committed")
+        actor._colocate_update_succeeded = True
+
+    actor.mark_colocate_update_committed = mark_committed
+    return actor
+
+
+def _run_load(events, actor, rollout, colocate=True, connected=False):
+    meta = SimpleNamespace(
+        type="awex",
+        colocate=colocate,
+        with_version=lambda v: SimpleNamespace(version=v, type="awex"),
+    )
+    recover_info = SimpleNamespace(
+        last_step_info=SimpleNamespace(global_step=7, next=lambda: "step-8"),
+        saver_info={},
+        evaluator_info={},
+        stats_logger_info={},
+        dataloader_info={},
+        checkpoint_info={},
+    )
+    noop = SimpleNamespace(load_state_dict=lambda _d: None)
+    with mock.patch("areal.utils.recover.RecoverInfo.load", return_value=recover_info):
+        return RecoverHandler.load(
+            _make_handler(events),
+            engine=actor,
+            saver=noop,
+            evaluator=noop,
+            stats_logger=noop,
+            dataloader=noop,
+            inference_engine=rollout,
+            weight_update_meta=meta,
+            inference_engine_connected=connected,
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("connected", [False, True])
+def test_recovery_restores_weights_and_versions_before_resuming(connected):
+    events = []
+    rollout = _make_rollout(events)
+    _run_load(events, _make_actor(events, rollout), rollout, connected=connected)
+
+    expected = [
+        ("offload", ("weights",)),
+        ("load_checkpoint", "default"),
+        ("update_weights", 8),
+        ("actor_set_version", 8),
+        ("rollout_set_version", 8),
+        "mark_committed",
+        ("onload", ("kv_cache",)),
+        "continue_generation",
+    ]
+    positions = [events.index(event) for event in expected]
+    assert positions == sorted(positions)
+    assert ("connect_engine" in events) is not connected
+
+
+def test_generation_stays_paused_when_checkpoint_load_fails():
+    events = []
+    rollout = _make_rollout(events)
+    actor = _make_actor(events, rollout)
+    handler = _make_handler(events)
+    handler._load_checkpoint = mock.Mock(side_effect=RuntimeError("checkpoint corrupt"))
+    with mock.patch(__name__ + "._make_handler", return_value=handler):
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="corrupt"):
+            _run_load(events, actor, rollout)
+
+    assert "continue_generation" not in events
+    assert "resume" not in events

+async def test_colocate_connect_reserves_session_and_quarantines_failed_init(
+    monkeypatch, outcome
+):
+    app = gateway_app.create_app()
+    app.state.http_session = object()
+    entered = asyncio.Event()
+    release = asyncio.Event()
+    init_calls = []
+
+    async def report(*args):
+        return {"ip": "192.0.2.1", "device_id": 0, "tp_size": 1, "pp_size": 1}
+
+    async def initialize(session, url, timeout, json_data):
+        init_calls.append(json_data["pair_name"])
+        if "train" in url:
+            entered.set()
+            await release.wait()
+            if outcome == "failure":
+                raise RuntimeError("training worker initialization failed")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gateway_app, "_get_json", report)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gateway_app, "_post", initialize)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gateway_app, "_ensure_meta_server", lambda app: "meta:1")
+    body = {
+        "pair_name": "a",
+        "train_worker_urls": ["http://train"],
+        "inference_worker_urls": ["http://infer"],
+        "mode": "awex",
+        "colocate": True,
+    }
+    transport = httpx.ASGITransport(app=app, raise_app_exceptions=False)
+    async with httpx.AsyncClient(
+        transport=transport, base_url="http://gateway", headers=_auth_headers()
+    ) as client:
+        first = asyncio.create_task(client.post("/connect", json=body))
+        try:
+            await asyncio.wait_for(entered.wait(), 5)
+            assert app.state.colocate_state == "connecting"
+            for name in ("a", "b"):
+                response = await client.post(
+                    "/connect", json={**body, "pair_name": name}
+                )
+                assert response.status_code == 409
+            assert init_calls == ["a", "a"]
+            if outcome == "cancelled":
+                first.cancel()
+                with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+                    await first
+            else:
+                release.set()
+                response = await first
+                assert response.status_code == (200 if outcome == "success" else 500)
+            expected = "active" if outcome == "success" else "failed"
+            assert app.state.colocate_state == expected
+            assert app.state.colocate_pair_name == "a"
+            for name in ("a", "b"):
+                response = await client.post(
+                    "/connect", json={**body, "pair_name": name}
+                )
+                assert response.status_code == (
+                    200 if outcome == "success" and name == "a" else 409
+                )
+            assert init_calls == ["a", "a"]
+            assert (app.state.registry.get_by_name("a") is not None) == (
+                outcome == "success"
+            )
+            assert app.state.registry.get_by_name("b") is None
+        finally:
+            release.set()
+            if not first.done():
+                first.cancel()
+            await asyncio.gather(first, return_exceptions=True)
